audits.claim: test_to_dict only checks that queued is present and therefore cannot detect its stale import-time default.
audits.evidence: tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:29-38 constructs a source without queued and asserts only that the serialized queued value is not None. src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 evaluates timezone.now() when the class is defined, and :27-28 serializes that same non-null datetime, so the assertion accepts the stale value. This is a concrete missing regression assertion, rather than a separate demonstrated runtime failure; finding 0 describes the underlying timestamp bug.

audits.claim: The new assignment-source loop prevention lacks tests for matching-source deassignment, inbound source forwarding, and a different source integration.
audits.evidence: tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:180-221 tests a matching source only through assign, while :269-275 tests deassign with assignment_source=None. Existing inbound tests at :321-347 and :380-388 assert assignment state, without asserting the forwarded source or suppressing a returning outbound call. The actual source forwarding is present in src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:94-115 and src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:238-240, and the equality-only guard at src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390-394 permits a different integration. Searching the checkout tests for AssignmentSource, assignment_source, and sync_source found no additional explicit source cases, so this is a valid coverage gap rather than evidence that those production paths are broken.
